subject: Post-incident: preservation scope, KMS custody, and retention timelines
messages:
From: Jake Mullins <jmullins@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 7 Sep 2025 15:21:00 +0000
Subject: Request: preserve logs + KMS custody clarity after Friday incident

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick coordination on Friday. We have one outstanding ask from our legal and ISA teams: they need formal confirmation of what artifacts Redwood will hold for forensic review and for how long. Specifically: 

- A full list of retained log sources (ingest, request traces, worker-side syslogs, KV cache persistence).
- Whether those artifacts will remain accessible in-region (US East) and for how long.
- Who controls the encryption keys for archived artifacts (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-owned).
- A chain-of-custody manifest (timestamps, checksums) we can reference during our audit.

Can you confirm an initial preservation window and whether you can provide the custody manifest template so we can align with our auditors? We may request an extension if our forensics partner needs more time.

Appreciate it — Jake
Security Operations
Acme Health

Attachment: incident_summary_acme_20250905.pdf (referenced)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Jake Mullins <jmullins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 7 Sep 2025 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: preserve logs + KMS custody clarity after Friday incident

Jake —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, then Ill loop in Aditya for technical specifics and Marissa for legal/SLAs.

1) Preservation window: Redwood will place a forensic hold on all candidate artifacts for an initial 90-day window starting 2025-09-05 21:40 UTC (time of containment). We can extend that window upon formal request from your legal/forensics team; please flag expected extension duration when you know it.

2) Sources preserved: request traces (api-gateway), application worker logs (worker nodes), model-serving inference traces (runtime KV snapshots), and telemetry captures correlated to the incident (sampling of tenant requestIDs). We will not automatically snapshot customer payloads beyond what is present in the traces unless requested and approved.

3) Key custody: by default archived artifacts are encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed keys in AWS KMS (us-east-1). If Acme needs customer-managed keys (CMK) for these particular artifacts we can escalate to a key-escrow flow but that requires a legal addendum and additional operational steps — Aditya, can you outline what that would mean for retrieval and chain-of-custody?

4) Chain-of-custody manifest: we have a template we use internally; Im attaching a cleaned version for your auditors (custody_manifest_template.xlsx). It includes object names, S3 paths, sha256 checksums, retrieval timestamps, and the operator who exported the slice.

Next steps: Aditya will send a technical note with exact object locations, retention flags, and a list of current key policies. Marissa will follow with the legal coordinates for the CMK addendum and any SLA implications.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: custody_manifest_template.xlsx (stub), internal_preserve_note.txt (internal only)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Jake Mullins <jmullins@acmehealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 09:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: preserve logs + KMS custody clarity after Friday incident

Kim / Jake —

Technical breakdown below; Ill keep it concise and flag follow-ups.

What we will snapshot and where:
- API gateway request traces: bucket redwood-forensics/us-east-1/acme-<tenant-id>/requests/2025-09-05/*.log (retention flag: forensic_hold=90d)
- Worker syslogs & stderr dumps: redwood-forensics/.../workers/20250905/* (compressed tar by node)
- Runtime KV cache dumps: stored as incremental checkpoints at s3://redwood-kv-dumps/us-east-1/acme-<tenant-id>/checkpoint-<ts>.chk
- Inference telemetry (sampled requestIDs): s3://redwood-telemetry-samples/acme-<tenant-id>/2025-09-05/sample.json

Encryption / keys:
- Current default: server-side encryption with AWS-managed keys (SSE-KMS, key id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/xxxxx). Redwood controls rotation and key policies.
- CMK flow: If Acme supplies a Customer Managed Key (a symmetric KMS key in your AWS account), we can configure cross-account encryption for the exported artifacts. This requires:
  * A legal addendum for key custody and export authorization.
  * A short maintenance window (we perform export jobs under a locked-forensics runbook).
  * HSM-backed export only if requested (adds ~48 hours to delivery).

Chain-of-custody and manifests:
- We generate sha256 checksums at export time and record an export entry in our audit index (export-id, operator, UTC timestamp). The manifest xlsx references these entries and S3 ETags. We can produce a signed manifest (GPG) upon request.

Retention vs deletion:
- Items under forensic_hold=90d will be read-only and excluded from normal lifecycle deletion jobs. After the hold expires we will either: 1) delete per standard lifecycle, or 2) extend the hold if requested.

Export sample:
- To give you something tangible, I attached a sanitized sample archive: log_extract_sample_20250907.tar.gz (contains two worker logs and a small KV checkpoint).

Let me know if you need the signed manifest and whether Acme will pursue CMK for long-term custody.

-Aditya
Inference Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: log_extract_sample_20250907.tar.gz (sanitized stub)

From: Carlos Vega <cvega@forensics-inc.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Jake Mullins <jmullins@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: preserve logs + KMS custody clarity after Friday incident

Kim / Aditya —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple of asks from the third-party forensics perspective: 

1) Please include the exact UTC timestamps used for each checkpoint and the algorithm used for checksums (sha256 is fine, please indicate block size if streaming).
2) Can you provide a lightweight chain-of-custody PDF (signed by the operator) with a GPG signature or similar? Our auditors prefer a signed artifact.
3) If export is done to Acme-provided CMK, wed like an attestation that keys were not re-wrapped or copied to other accounts during the process.

If possible, please respond with the expected delivery ETA for a signed manifest and the PDF chain-of-custody. Were coordinating a slot for evidence ingestion on Thursday, so 48-72h turnaround would be ideal.

Regards,
Carlos Vega
Lead Forensic Analyst
Forensics, Inc.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Jake Mullins <jmullins@acmehealth.com>, legal-escalations@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: preserve logs + KMS custody clarity after Friday incident

Looping legal — FYI: Ive drafted a CMK addendum and a short attestation template that covers the non-repudiation language Carlos requests. I can run this through the partner SLA workflow today; expect a DocuSign link in the next 24 hours.

Operationally: Aditya, please prepare the signed manifest (GPG) and a PDF chain-of-custody (operator-signed). Target: EOD Wednesday (2025-09-10) for delivery to Acme’s ingest window on Thursday. If CMK is selected, include the key ARN and a short attestation that no re-wrapping occurred during export.

Kimberly / Jake: once DocuSign is sent, well pause deletion beyond the 90-day window until the addendum is complete per Acmes request.

Thanks — Marissa
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Related links: https://redwood.example.com/docs/incident-retention-playbook
Attachments: custody_manifest_template.xlsx (sent earlier)
